name: Planning Data brownfield land dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 37,666 brownfield land records from 354 providers; collector last ran 20 July 2026 and all data is from authoritative sources.
gate: Register inclusion identifies development-potential land, not a current permission, land-control agreement or canonical parcel relation.

name: Planning Data brownfield site experimental dataset
fact: Experimental boundary dataset has 2,916 sites from five providers; collector ran 23 July 2026 and origin is MHCLG-created pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Do not use experimental boundaries as exact parcel geometry or authoritative register status.

name: Planning Data ownership status taxonomy
fact: Four authoritative ownership states are published: public, non-public, mixed and unknown.
gate: Ownership class does not prove control, willingness to sell, vacant possession or development availability.

name: Planning Data planning permission status taxonomy
fact: Current taxonomy has permissioned, not-permissioned and pending-decision; collector last ran 23 July 2026.
gate: Status must be read with the exact site record and live planning history; pending-decision is not consent.

name: Planning Data datasets index
fact: Current Planning Data catalogue exposes site, legal-instrument, policy, heritage and infrastructure-related datasets and controlled vocabularies.
gate: Catalogue discovery is not parcel evidence by itself.

name: Create or update a local plan using the new system
fact: The 2026 local-plan regulations are in force from 25 March 2026; the collection was updated 6 July 2026 and organises the new gateway, site-selection and data-publication process.
gate: Guidance describes plan preparation and does not make any individual site an allocation.

name: Plan-making and local government reorganisation
fact: Published 6 July 2026; draft guidance describes transitional plan-making for authorities moving to unitary structures.
gate: It is expressly draft and subject to change; do not treat it as final policy or parcel status.

name: Roadmap of resources and support for new local plans
fact: Updated 19 May 2026; MHCLG roadmap tracks tools, gateway guidance, evidence, data and funding for the new plan-making system.
gate: Roadmap availability is process context only.

name: 30-month local plan process overview
fact: Updated 26 March 2026; process includes notice, scoping, Gateways 1-3, examination, adoption and monitoring, with a minimum four-month notice before preparation.
gate: Process timing does not establish site allocation, permission or deliverability.

name: Gateway 1 for local plans
fact: Published 23 June 2026; Gateway 1 is the self-assessment step for readiness to enter the 30-month plan-preparation process.
gate: Gateway readiness is plan-level evidence, not an individual development approval.

name: Gateway 2 assessment for local plans
fact: Published 22 June 2026; an assessor reviews progress, evidence, conformity and soundness issues and the LPA must have regard to the report.
gate: Gateway advice can change plan content; it is not a site permission.

name: Gateway 3 for local plans
fact: Published 22 June 2026; Gateway 3 checks readiness to submit a local plan for examination.
gate: Passing Gateway 3 does not itself adopt the plan or grant site permission.

name: Identifying, assessing and selecting sites introduction
fact: Current guidance sets a four-stage process: identify, assess, determine draft allocations, then confirm allocations and record decisions.
gate: Potential-site identification is not allocation or permission.

name: Stage 1 identifying sites
fact: Stage 1 requires a thorough audit of available land and says constraints do not need to be applied yet because sites are only being identified for later assessment.
gate: Stage-1 inclusion must never be promoted as suitability, allocation or consent.

name: Stage 2 assessing sites
fact: Stage 2 covers categorisation, suitability, availability, achievability, development potential and scoring.
gate: Assessment outputs remain plan evidence and require later allocation and plan adoption before policy status is inferred.

name: Stage 4 confirming draft allocations
fact: Stage 4 produces draft allocations, rejected-site lists, rationales, evidence and RAG scores for the proposed plan.
gate: A draft allocation remains subject to consultation and examination and is not planning permission.

name: Publishing local plan housing requirement
fact: Updated 13 May 2026; LPAs must publish housing requirement data at proposed-plan consultation, examination submission, examiner recommendations and adoption.
gate: Housing requirement is area-level demand evidence, not parcel capacity.

name: NPPF delivering a sufficient supply of homes
fact: National policy requires identification and annual updating of deliverable housing sites; from 1 July 2026 it adds a specified 20% buffer case for decision-making.
gate: Five-year supply and buffer policy affect decisions but do not create consent or prove a site's deliverability.

name: PINS new-style local plan examination process
fact: Published 18 June 2026; Planning Inspectorate guidance describes examination under the 2026 plan system.
gate: Examination procedure is not an adopted policy or parcel decision.

name: PINS procedural guide for examinations and gateways
fact: Current guide explains Gateways 1-3 and examination and states the evidence base should be complete before Gateway 3.
gate: Procedure and readiness evidence do not create a development permission.

name: National Housing Delivery Fund - MHCLG
fact: Published 31 March 2026; NHDF supports infrastructure and land intended to accelerate net additional housing and brownfield delivery.
gate: Programme eligibility or policy priority is not evidence of a site award.

name: National Housing Delivery Fund - Homes England
fact: Homes England and National Housing Bank guidance says NHDF can support land assembly, remediation, utilities, schools, grants, debt, equity and guarantees.
gate: Availability of support is not a signed funding agreement or site viability proof.

name: National Housing Delivery Fund information collection
fact: Current collection groups NHDF guidance, enquiry, due-diligence and contact material.
gate: Collection membership is programme context only.

name: National Housing Bank
fact: Published 31 March 2026; the government-backed National Housing Bank is intended to unlock housing, infrastructure and regeneration investment.
gate: Bank existence does not prove finance for a particular site.

name: National Housing Bank structured finance
fact: Structured finance can support complex development, infrastructure, land acquisition and multi-site lending.
gate: Product availability is not a credit decision, signed facility or parcel-level viability result.

name: National Housing Bank affordable housing loans
fact: Published 31 March 2026; £2.5bn low-interest lending programme supports social and affordable housing, with a 0.1% interest rate and 25-year term described in guidance.
gate: Programme terms do not imply any project has been awarded funding.
